content.content:
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- **Deliverables.** A finished file made for someone else this session (PDF, deck, report, sheet) gets a copy at `~/DEV/_DRIVE/03_REPORTS/YYYY-MM-DD_<Sport>_<Topic>_<Audience>.<ext>`. The repo keeps the source; Drive keeps the handed-off copy. Name the copy in the report.
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. If not empty, surface it and fix the hook issue if obvious, then append its lines to `transcripts/.errors.log.archived-<YYYY-MM-DD>` and clear it with `cp /dev/null` (same archive-then-clear step as backup and claude-stack-doctor; `: > file` is dcg-blocked).
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric, each one written out in full as its own top-level bullet: the question itself and enough context to answer it without opening another file. Never a pointer ("See PLAN.md"): `/startup` reads this section across every repo with `where-was-i.py --decisions`, and a pointer gives no question to answer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …` or strike them through (`~~…~~`) so they drop off that list. Leave the section empty, not "-", when nothing is waiting.
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

Then run `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1`. It prints exactly what tomorrow's `/startup` will show as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision this session left open must appear there as a readable question; if one is missing or shows as a pointer, fix that repo's `## Open questions` before the commit.

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Monthly: append AIOS metrics to the trend table and nudge for a real audit.
# Deliberately does NOT commit, push, or run the agentic audit (see R9):
#  - committing from the shared tree would publish the user's staged files
#  - the agentic audit proposes deletions and needs a human reading them
set -uo pipefail

REPO="$HOME/DEV/KeystoneOS"
TREND="$REPO/docs/audits/aios-trend.md"
LOG="$HOME/.claude/scripts/logs/aios-audit.log"
LOCK="$HOME/.claude/scripts/.aios-audit.lock"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")" "$(dirname "$TREND")" "$HOME/.claude/global-memory/transcripts"

exec >>"$LOG" 2>&1
echo "=== $(date -u +%FT%TZ) aios-audit-cron ==="

# Single-instance lock. mkdir is atomic; no flock on stock macOS.
# R2-06: a kill or reboot must not wedge every future run. The lock records
# its owner PID; a lock whose owner is gone, or that is older than a day, is
# stale and gets reclaimed.
#
# Gate C C-02: reclaiming is serialised by a second atomic lock, $RECOVER.
# Without it, two runs could both judge the same dead owner stale; the second
# run's rm -rf then deleted the first run's fresh lock and both wrote rows.
# Only a holder of $RECOVER may delete $LOCK. Ownership is re-read while
# holding it. Residual risk, accepted: a crash inside the few-millisecond
# recovery section, followed >10 min later by two runs starting together.
RECOVER="$LOCK.recover"

owner_of_lock() { cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null; }

# Returns 0 if the lock has no pid file and is younger than a day. That is a
# live run between its mkdir and its pid write - never reclaim it.
young_ownerless() {
  local owner="$1" old
  old="$(find "$LOCK" -maxdepth 0 -mtime +1 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
  [ -z "$owner" ] && [ "$old" = "0" ]
}

content.thinking:
The .windows.md handoff twins seem like dead duplicates with no active writer. The daily_extract.log file is actually tracked and committed daily by the graphextract script itself, not through stdout redirection, so it's accumulating as a growing history in git.

Now I'm starting to build out the structured output, cataloging each location with its status, size, writer, and reader, working through the audits directory first -- covering the active audit reports and recall-eval logs, the stale skills-audit files, the KeystoneOS docs/audits that get harvested into dev-docs, and the stale os-audits from July.

I'm continuing through SecondBrain's active brain-audit reports, the claude-memory-compiler's weekly memlint reports and stale health-history log, the doctor-plus backups, and now moving into the handoffs directory with its 212K of active handoff files.

Then there's the per-repo docs/handoffs setup across 38 repos with 142 files, which is the canonical source read by where-was-i and harvest scripts, versus the claude-global-memory handoffs fallback with its 126 entries and duplicate .windows.md twins that isn't indexed anywhere—plus a duplicate claude-global-memory checkout sitting elsewhere.

I'm also noting the dev-docs cache as a regenerable duplicate with 158 directories and 43 orphaned archived-repo copies, alongside stray handoff clutter and some non-durable temp/session files. Then checking the STATUS.md file's current size and entry count, and starting to look at the docs/handoffs directory itself.

Across the repos, there's a wide range of active STATUS.md files, with Flint and TypeSafe_Sandbox having the largest, plus smaller active status trackers scattered across the .claude directories and skills folders. The HARNESS_FIXES.md file is still somewhat active at 4.4K, and I'm now moving into checking the global-memory directory next.

23. Looking at the landed/*.jsonl files, these are actively tracked across three machines totaling 1.6M, with the Mac entries being the bulk of the data and Windows machine data from the closeout scan.

24. The run-ledger.json for KeystoneOS is active but gitignored at 27K.

25. There's a case mismatch issue with the RTP_WorkingGroup STATUS.md path.

26. Now checking the logs directory — 4.2M across 45 files, gitignored, with the daily-backup.log self-capping at 2MB and a large cloud-push binary file that got rewritten.

27. The errors.log channel is active with zero bytes currently but has 30+ writers feeding into it and the snapshot script reading from it.

28. The transcript error archives are stale clutter at 37 files and 208K total.

29. autopush.log is minimal, just a few lines from the session-autopush writer.

30. The compiler scripts' flush/compile/adjudicate logs are active and growing unbounded without rotation.

31. The permission-gate shadow.jsonl is substantial at 5.5M across 18,620 lines since September 22nd with no rotation, written by the PreToolUse hook.

32. skill_router.log is also unrotated, 116K since September 21st.

33. daemon.log is app-managed, around 230K since August.

34. In context-mode, the heal-partial-install log is actively growing at 596K from the plugin, while the other logs there are stale leftovers from Windows.

Now I'm moving on to more system-wide logs: everythingd.log is actively flooding with 27,037 'giving up' lines totaling 5.5M, growing fast from its 3MB baseline a month ago with no rotation configured for the launchd daemon. Claude's own logs self-rotate properly at 55M. OneDrive, Codex, and their associated databases are all large but app-managed, so they're not my concern. Looking at the DEV project logs now — KeystoneOS has scattered job outputs, cadence logs, and inventory files all gitignored and unpruned; several repo-local pipeline logs are mid-season and should be left alone; graphify-out's daily extract log is actually tracked and committed to git, which is unusual. I'm also noting some dead log paths in /tmp and CommandCentre that may no longer be relevant.

Now shifting to backup clutter: there's a sizable collection of Claude settings backups, rolling json backups updating every minute, stale doctor and skills backups from mid-year, and a batch of tracked .bak files in dotclaude that are essentially duplicating git history unnecessarily. I'm also seeing backup files scattered across LaunchAgents plists and Codex hooks configs.

Beyond backups, there's a large _windows-import-archive at 930M that's stale, and a huge 28G _PARKED_COPIES folder already covered by an existing file-organization plan. Now I'm ranking the actual problems: the top issue is that handoff documents live in three different locations, two of which tooling can't see, so recall and status checks silently miss them — the fix is to standardize on one workspace-level path, freeze the old global-memory location as historical, and extend the indexing and "where-was-i" tooling to cover the new root.

Next is STATUS.md bloating across the fleet since the closeout rule limiting entries isn't enforced anywhere except the DEV root — I want to generalize the archiving logic so any status file over a size or entry threshold automatically splits older entries into quarterly archive files, rolling this out to a few projects first as a low-risk docs move.

Then there's the errors-log archiving problem: files are getting zeroed out or lost entirely, there are 37 archive files across six different naming conventions, and some skills overwrite with `cp` while the closeout process expects appends — I'm thinking the fix is a single append-only ledger file that all tools write to consistently.

After that, unrotated logs are ballooning in size daily (everythingd, shadow.jsonl, heal, flush, cadence, inventory), so I want a small rotation helper script that trims any oversized log to its tail, plus addressing the root cause of everythingd's growth by excluding FileProvider paths, while avoiding touching system-level newsyslog config since that needs sudo.

For P5, dev-docs never prunes and ends up with 43 orphan folders for archived or renamed repos, including local-only repos like Linda_Projects that harvest doesn't currently guard against — the fix is to rsync with delete per repo, remove dev-docs entries when the source is gone, and add local-only repos to a skip list, since dev-docs is regenerable so a full wipe-and-rebuild is low risk (just let the next scheduled memsearch index pick up the change rather than forcing a rebuild).

P6 is a stale duplicate clone of claude-global-memory (16M, 26 commits behind) that's been harvested as a second home for 125 handoffs and referenced in PLATFORM.md as the global memory repo — the fix is to remove the clone or replace it with a symlink to the real global-memory location, then update PLATFORM.md, the backup manifest, and the digest script, though this carries medium risk since other paths may reference it.

P7 covers audit reports scattered across 6+ locations with no consistent rule — the fix is to establish ~/.claude/audits/YYYY-MM-DD-topic.md as the canonical home for one-off audits while leaving script-bound audit directories like KeystoneOS/docs/audits and SecondBrain/audits in place since they're tied to specific tooling.

Now I'm looking at P8: config backup clutter spread across untracked settings backups, tracked .bak files in dotclaude and global-memory, plist backups, and various other redundant copies totaling significant disk space — since git history already preserves these files, the fix is to delete most of the untracked backups, remove the tracked .bak files from git, add a .bak* ignore rule, and establish a clear convention that manual pre-change copies belong in a dedicated backups/manual directory organized by date.

P9 covers dead handoff duplicate files in tracked global-memory with no active writer, fixed simply by removing them from git while keeping history. P10 addresses a landed ledger fragmented across two hostname variants for the same Mac, fixed by keying the ledger on a stable machine identifier, merging the duplicate files, and adding a size cap. P11 catalogs stale and dead log files across scripts/logs and plists — zero-byte stubs, old error logs, retired digest outputs, moved plist targets, and stale per-run job outputs.

I'm now looking at P12, a daily-committed git-tracked extract log that should be gitignored and removed from the cache, P13 covering a large stale Windows import archive that needs a hash-diff check before deletion (Eric's call given irreversibility), and a note that the Claude backup file rotation is already bounded and not an issue. I'm also compiling a short not-checked list — drive mount contents, a couple of unopened project directories, and the unconfirmed writers behind a few backup files — before drafting the overall summary.

Every kind of record has a canonical-looking home: <repo>/docs/handoffs, <repo>/docs/STATUS.md, ~/.claude/scripts/logs plus the one alert channel .errors.log, and git history for config. Growth is mostly unbounded: only daily-backup.ps1 caps its own log. everythingd.log went from 3.0 to 5.5 MB in about a day, shadow.jsonl from 4.6 to 5.6 MB, and STATUS bloat is a fleet problem (Flint 87 KB, TypeSafe_Sandbox 55 KB, PP_Recruiting 38 KB), while only the DEV root got an archive on 10-23. problems.title: Handoffs have three live homes, and two of them are invisible to the tools that surface handoffs
problems.evidence: Live writes on 10-23 went to /Users/kristinarash/DEV/docs/handoffs (2026-10-23-audit-followup.md and 3 more), /Users/kristinarash/.claude/global-memory/handoffs (2026-10-23-weekly-review-no-movement.md) and <repo>/docs/handoffs (142 files in 38 repos). where-was-i.py recent_handoffs() uses dev_glob('docs','handoffs','*.md') = DEV/*/docs/handoffs and DEV/*/*/docs/handoffs, which never matches DEV/docs/handoffs. harvest-dev-docs.sh iterates DEV/<x>/docs only. KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json (the recall.py and memsearch roots) lists neither ~/DEV/docs nor ~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs. closeout SKILL.md:57 sends work to global-memory/handoffs 'if no repo fits', but the DEV root is itself a repo.
problems.impact: The workspace-level and cross-project handoffs, often the most important ones, cannot be found by /where-was-i, /startup or recall. Sessions guess which folder to use, so the split keeps growing.
problems.suggested_fix: Rule: a handoff goes in <repo>/docs/handoffs, and workspace or system work goes in ~/DEV/docs/handoffs. Change closeout's fallback from global-memory/handoffs to ~/DEV/docs/handoffs, and treat global-memory/handoffs as read-only history (no new files). Add '{DEV}/docs' and '{HOME}/.claude/global-memory/handoffs' to memory-index-paths.json, and have where-was-i.py also glob os.path.join(DEV,'docs','handoffs','*.md') and DEV/docs/STATUS.md.

problems.title: STATUS.md bloat is fleet-wide; only the DEV root got an archive, and closeout's 'two to five lines' rule is not enforced
problems.evidence: DEV root is now 34,139 B / 157 lines / 26 dated entries (was 266 / 39 KB on 10-22; the archive STATUS-archive-2026-Q3.md landed 10-23). Larger than the root ever was: Flint/docs/STATUS.md 86,897 B / 527 lines, TypeSafe_Sandbox 54,948 / 657, PP_Recruiting 38,371 / 535; next are sleep-scheduler 23K, project-triage 23K, CFB_Playoff_Benchmarks 21K and _INBOX 19K. find for '*STATUS*archive*' in DEV finds only the root archive. closeout SKILL.md:67-69 says 'Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short ... two to five lines', but in practice sessions append dated 1-3 KB entries. Known for the root only as 10-22 audit id dev-root-status-bloat.
problems.impact: Every session reads these first (tens of thousands of tokens for Flint or TypeSafe), and stale NEXT items mislead /startup, card-check and cloud sessions.
problems.suggested_fix: Apply the DEV-root move to every repo through closeout: when '## Current state' has more than 15 dated entries or the file is over 20 KB, move entries older than 14 days verbatim to <repo>/docs/handoffs/STATUS-archive-<YYYY>-Q<n>.md, then prune done Next items. Do Flint, TypeSafe_Sandbox and PP_Recruiting by hand once. Treat PP_Recruiting as football-adjacent: archive text only, no structural change mid-season.

problems.title: The .errors.log archive-then-clear step still loses alerts after the 10-23 fix, and the archives use 6 naming patterns
problems.evidence: Commit 5712b7c (10-23 15:51) shows 9 'transcript_path does not exist' lines in transcripts/.errors.log, and c77efe0 (16:58) removes them. transcripts/.errors.log.archived-2026-10-23 is 0 bytes (mtime 16:14) and was committed empty, so those lines survive only in git. The skills disagree: closeout SKILL.md:46 says 'append'; backup SKILL.md:43 and claude-stack-doctor SKILL.md:89 use 'cp .errors.log .errors.log.archived-$(date)', which overwrites a same-day archive. There are 37 archive files (208K) in 6 patterns: .errors-archive-<d>.log, .errors.log.archive-<d>, .errors.log.archived-<d>[b|-closeout], .errors.log.bak-<d>, errors-archive-<d>.log and errors-archive-2026-08-to-09.log. Known as 10-22 audit id mp-errors-log-alerts-lost; the loss repeated after the fix.
problems.impact: Alerts such as a failed flush, a backup error or a cloud-push ERROR can disappear before Eric sees the pattern. The archives are hard to read as a history.
problems.suggested_fix: Use one append-only ledger: transcripts/.errors-ledger.log. Put the step in a tiny script (cat .errors.log >> .errors-ledger.log && cp /dev/null .errors.log) and call it from closeout, backup and claude-stack-doctor instead of three hand-written variants. Optionally concatenate the 37 old archives into the ledger once and git rm them (git keeps the history).

problems.title: Only daily-backup.ps1 caps its own log; the other fast-growing logs have no rotation
problems.evidence: /Users/kristinarash/Library/Logs/everythingd.log is 5,534,235 B (3.0 MB at the 10-22 audit, so about 2.5 MB in a day) with 27,037 'giving up' FileProvider lines. /Users/kristinarash/.claude/permission-gate/shadow.jsonl is 5,559,889 B / 18,620 lines (4.6 MB / 15,630 lines on 10-22). context-mode/heal-partial-install.log is 606,889 B (579 KB on 10-22). KeystoneOS/outputs/morning/cadence.log is 570,716 B. claude-memory-compiler/scripts/flush.log is 400,080 B since 08-05. skill_router.log is 116,379 B since 09-21. KeystoneOS/outputs/inventory is 7.5 MB / 204 files at ~125 KB/day. daily-backup.ps1:809 is the only rotation found (>2MB -> keep tail 2000). A grep for rotation in the compiler scripts, cloud-push.py, permission-gate and the hooks found nothing. Known in part as 10-22 audit ids sched-everythingd-fileprovider-crawl, settings-hooks-shadow-gate-unreviewed, settings-hooks-cleanup-cruft and disksec-misc-stale-state.
problems.impact: Disk and attention waste. everythingd's growth is a symptom of the Drive FUSE crawl that the Drive read-hang memory warns about.
problems.suggested_fix: Fix everythingd's cause first: exclude ~/Library/Application Support/FileProvider and ~/Library/CloudStorage from its index roots. Then add one small rotate step to daily-backup.ps1 (it already runs daily and has the pattern): a list of paths (shadow.jsonl, everythingd.log, heal-partial-install.log, flush.log, compile.log, cadence.log, skill_router.log, daily-backup.out), each trimmed to its last N lines when over 2 MB, and prune KeystoneOS outputs/inventory and outputs/jobs files older than 60 days. Avoid /etc/newsyslog.d, which is a system setting.

problems.title: The harvested dev-docs mirror never prunes, so archived repos stay indexed as live; it also has no local-only guard
problems.evidence: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs has 158 folders, and 43 have no source in DEV, DEV/Football or DEV/SpecialRequests. Examples: InjurPred, VALD_analytics, AI_Analyst, CommandCentre, morning-briefing and SprintLab are now in ~/DEV/_ARCHIVE (27 repos moved there on 10-23); 'Gemini Projects' and Gemini_Projects are rename twins. harvest-dev-docs.sh runs rsync -a without --delete and never removes a folder whose repo is gone. Its skip list is only _DRIVE|_tools|.claude|graphify-out. dev-docs/Linda_Projects and dev-docs/'Linda Projects' exist (contents not opened). dev-docs is a memsearch and recall.py root.
problems.impact: Recall and memsearch return stale STATUS and handoffs from parked repos as current. Local-only project docs are copied into an indexed tree under ~/.claude (gitignored, so not pushed to GitHub).
problems.suggested_fix: Make the harvest a true mirror: rsync --delete per repo, and remove dev-docs/<name> when the source folder is gone. It is regenerable, so wiping and re-harvesting is safe. Add a local-only skip (Linda_Projects, SpecialRequests/TOS_ES, DexaProject, and any repo whose CLAUDE.md says 'local only'). Larger than the root ever was: Flint/docs/STATUS.md 86,897 B / 527 lines, TypeSafe_Sandbox 54,948 / 657, PP_Recruiting 38,371 / 535; next are sleep-scheduler 23K, project-triage 23K, CFB_Playoff_Benchmarks 21K and _INBOX 19K. find for '*STATUS*archive*' in DEV finds only the root archive. closeout SKILL.md:67-69 says 'Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short ... two to five lines', but in practice sessions append dated 1-3 KB entries. problems.suggested_fix: Apply the DEV-root move to every repo through closeout: when '## Current state' has more than 15 dated entries or the file is over 20 KB, move entries older than 14 days verbatim to <repo>/docs/handoffs/STATUS-archive-<YYYY>-Q<n>.md, then prune done Next items. Do Flint, TypeSafe_Sandbox and PP_Recruiting by hand once. Treat PP_Recruiting as football-adjacent: archive text only, no structural change mid-season.

problems.title: The .errors.log archive-then-clear step still loses alerts after the 10-23 fix, and the archives use 6 naming patterns
problems.evidence: Commit 5712b7c (10-23 15:51) shows 9 'transcript_path does not exist' lines in transcripts/.errors.log, and c77efe0 (16:58) removes them. transcripts/.errors.log.archived-2026-10-23 is 0 bytes (mtime 16:14) and was committed empty, so those lines survive only in git. The skills disagree: closeout SKILL.md:46 says 'append'; backup SKILL.md:43 and claude-stack-doctor SKILL.md:89 use 'cp .errors.log .errors.log.archived-$(date)', which overwrites a same-day archive. There are 37 archive files (208K) in 6 patterns: .errors-archive-<d>.log, .errors.log.archive-<d>, .errors.log.archived-<d>[b|-closeout], .errors.log.bak-<d>, errors-archive-<d>.log and errors-archive-2026-08-to-09.log. Known as 10-22 audit id mp-errors-log-alerts-lost; the loss repeated after the fix.
problems.impact: Alerts such as a failed flush, a backup error or a cloud-push ERROR can disappear before Eric sees the pattern. The archives are hard to read as a history.
problems.suggested_fix: Use one append-only ledger: transcripts/.errors-ledger.log. Put the step in a tiny script (cat .errors.log >> .errors-ledger.log && cp /dev/null .errors.log) and call it from closeout, backup and claude-stack-doctor instead of three hand-written variants. Optionally concatenate the 37 old archives into the ledger once and git rm them (git keeps the history).

problems.title: Only daily-backup.ps1 caps its own log; the other fast-growing logs have no rotation
problems.evidence: /Users/kristinarash/Library/Logs/everythingd.log is 5,534,235 B (3.0 MB at the 10-22 audit, so about 2.5 MB in a day) with 27,037 'giving up' FileProvider lines. /Users/kristinarash/.claude/permission-gate/shadow.jsonl is 5,559,889 B / 18,620 lines (4.6 MB / 15,630 lines on 10-22). context-mode/heal-partial-install.log is 606,889 B (579 KB on 10-22). KeystoneOS/outputs/morning/cadence.log is 570,716 B. claude-memory-compiler/scripts/flush.log is 400,080 B since 08-05. skill_router.log is 116,379 B since 09-21. KeystoneOS/outputs/inventory is 7.5 MB / 204 files at ~125 KB/day. daily-backup.ps1:809 is the only rotation found (>2MB -> keep tail 2000). A grep for rotation in the compiler scripts, cloud-push.py, permission-gate and the hooks found nothing. Known in part as 10-22 audit ids sched-everythingd-fileprovider-crawl, settings-hooks-shadow-gate-unreviewed, settings-hooks-cleanup-cruft and disksec-misc-stale-state.
problems.impact: Disk and attention waste. everythingd's growth is a symptom of the Drive FUSE crawl that the Drive read-hang memory warns about.
problems.suggested_fix: Fix everythingd's cause first: exclude ~/Library/Application Support/FileProvider and ~/Library/CloudStorage from its index roots. Then add one small rotate step to daily-backup.ps1 (it already runs daily and has the pattern): a list of paths (shadow.jsonl, everythingd.log, heal-partial-install.log, flush.log, compile.log, cadence.log, skill_router.log, daily-backup.out), each trimmed to its last N lines when over 2 MB, and prune KeystoneOS outputs/inventory and outputs/jobs files older than 60 days. Avoid /etc/newsyslog.d, which is a system setting.

problems.title: The harvested dev-docs mirror never prunes, so archived repos stay indexed as live; it also has no local-only guard
problems.evidence: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs has 158 folders, and 43 have no source in DEV, DEV/Football or DEV/SpecialRequests. Examples: InjurPred, VALD_analytics, AI_Analyst, CommandCentre, morning-briefing and SprintLab are now in ~/DEV/_ARCHIVE (27 repos moved there on 10-23); 'Gemini Projects' and Gemini_Projects are rename twins. harvest-dev-docs.sh runs rsync -a without --delete and never removes a folder whose repo is gone. Its skip list is only _DRIVE|_tools|.claude|graphify-out. dev-docs/Linda_Projects and dev-docs/'Linda Projects' exist (contents not opened). dev-docs is a memsearch and recall.py root.
problems.impact: Recall and memsearch return stale STATUS and handoffs from parked repos as current. Local-only project docs are copied into an indexed tree under ~/.claude (gitignored, so not pushed to GitHub).
problems.suggested_fix: Make the harvest a true mirror: rsync --delete per repo, and remove dev-docs/<name> when the source folder is gone. It is regenerable, so wiping and re-harvesting is safe. Add a local-only skip (Linda_Projects, SpecialRequests/TOS_ES, DexaProject, and any repo whose CLAUDE.md says 'local only'). Let the next scheduled memsearch index pick up the change; do not run 'memsearch index' by hand (the destructive-index memory).

problems.title: Config backups are scattered ad-hoc copies that duplicate git history
problems.evidence: Top level of ~/.claude: 16 untracked files totalling 372K: settings.json.bak (9 variants), settings.json.lifeos-backup-1783558458907, settings-backup-r1mu_1t3.json, claude-json-backup-teppjgm3.json, AGENTS.md.bak-2026-08-29, CLAUDE.md.bak-2026-08-29, machine.md.encoding-bak, .gitignore.bak-20260909-154417. dotclaude has 24 tracked .bak/.win-orig files today (29 at the 10-22 audit): backup-manifest.json.bak x14, daily-backup.ps1.bak x6 + .win-orig, memsearch-sync.js.bak x3. global-memory tracks MEMORY.md.bak x2 and .errors.log.bak. Elsewhere: doctor-backup-20260807-135924 (23M), skills-backup-20260609 (244K), skill-router/roster.json.bak-20260921 (262K), 3 LaunchAgents dailybackup .bak, ~/.codex hooks.json.bak.20260815093235 and 2 ..codex-global-state tmp files. No code writer was found for the random-suffix files. Known as 10-22 audit ids disksec-bak-file-clutter and settings-hooks-cleanup-cruft.
problems.impact: A grep or a restore can hit a stale copy, and the clutter hides the real backups.
problems.suggested_fix: Rule: the backup of a config file is its git history plus the daily Drive tgz. Before a risky edit, commit first; if a loose copy is unavoidable, put it in ~/.claude/backups/manual/<date>/ and delete it after 30 days. Then git rm the 24 tracked .bak files and the 3 in global-memory, delete the untracked top-level copies, and add '*.bak*' and '*.orig' to the whitelisted dirs' ignore rules. Remove doctor-backup-20260807-135924 and skills-backup-20260609 after confirming nothing in them is needed. Leave ~/.claude/backups/.claude.json.backup.* alone (the app rolls 5).
